title.zh: 卷448 列傳二百三十五 丁日昌 卞宝第 涂宗瀛 黎培敬 崧骏 崧蕃 边宝泉 于荫霖 饶应祺 恽祖翼
title.en: Volume 448 Biographies 235: Ding Richang, Bian Baodi, Tu Zong Ying, Li Peijing, Song Jun, Song Fan, Bian Baoquan, Yu Yinlin, Rao Yingqi, Yun Zu Yi
title.raw: 卷448 列傳二百三十五 丁日昌 卞宝第 涂宗瀛 黎培敬 崧骏 崧蕃 边宝泉 于荫霖 饶应祺 恽祖翼

sentences.zh: 丁日昌，字禹生，廣東豐順人。

translations.literal: Ding Richang, style name Yusheng, was a native of Fengshun, Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Richang, whose courtesy name was Yusheng, came from Fengshun in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 以廩貢生治鄉團，數卻潮州寇。

translations.literal: As a stipend-supported licentiate graduate he managed local militia and several times repelled Chaozhou bandits.
translations.idiomatic: While still a licentiate on stipend, he organized village defense corps and repeatedly drove off raiders from Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 選瓊州府學訓導。

translations.literal: He was selected as Director of Studies for the Qiongzhou Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed instructor at the Qiongzhou prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 錄功敘知縣，補江西萬安，善折獄。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded and he was nominated as magistrate; he was assigned to Wan'an in Jiangxi and was skilled at deciding lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for his service, he was slated for a magistracy and posted to Wan'an in Jiangxi, where he proved adept at settling legal disputes.

sentences.zh: 坐吉安不守，罷免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for failing to hold Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his post when Ji'an fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 參曾國籓戎幕，复官。

translations.literal: He joined Zeng Guofan's military staff and was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zeng Guofan's headquarters as a staff officer and regained his official rank.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章治軍上海，檄主機器局，積勳至知府。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang raised troops at Shanghai, he was ordered to head the Arsenal Bureau and, through accumulated merit, rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang's campaign in Shanghai brought him orders to run the machine works; his accumulated service eventually earned him the rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 江寧既下，除蘇松太道。

translations.literal: After Jiangning was taken, he was appointed Intendant of Su-Song-Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Once Nanjing had been captured, he was made intendant of the Suzhou–Songjiang–Taicang circuit.

sentences.zh: 鴻章倚以辦外交，事有鉤棘，徐起應付，率皆就範。

translations.literal: Hongzhang relied on him for foreign affairs; when matters were tangled, he would rise slowly to deal with them and they generally came within bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang leaned on him for diplomacy. Even knotty negotiations, which Ding handled with deliberate calm, usually ended within acceptable limits.

sentences.zh: 調兩淮鹽運使，淮鹽故弊藪，至則禁私販，糾貪吏，鬯運道，歲入驟增。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Salt Transport Commissioner for the Liang-Huai circuit; Huai salt had long been a nest of abuses, but on his arrival he banned private trade, punished corrupt officials, cleared the transport routes, and annual receipts surged.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to commissioner of Liang-Huai salt, he found a trade riddled with corruption. He suppressed smuggling, punished venal officials, and opened the transport channels, and revenue jumped within the year.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，擢布政使，授巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Tongzhi reign he was promoted to provincial treasurer and then appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi year six he rose to provincial treasurer and was then made governor.

sentences.zh: 江南戎燼後，庶政不緝，日昌集流亡，除豪猾，設月報詞訟冊，定錢漕科則，下其法各省；

translations.literal: After the war fires in Jiangnan, civil administration was in disorder; Richang gathered the displaced, removed powerful ruffians, instituted monthly litigation registers, fixed rates for land tax and grain transport, and sent his regulations down to every province.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan lay in ruins after the war, and government had fallen slack. Ding resettled refugees, broke the power of local bullies, required monthly reports on lawsuits, standardized land-tax and grain quotas, and had his methods adopted province by province.

sentences.zh: 又以州縣為親民官，疏請設局編刻牧令諸書。

translations.literal: He also held that prefects and magistrates were the officials closest to the people and memorialized to set up a bureau to compile and print books for local administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Believing that county and prefectural magistrates were the officials who truly touched people's lives, he asked the court to establish a bureau to edit and publish handbooks for local rule.

sentences.zh: 八年，奉敕訓勉臣工，日昌條上六事，曰：舉賢才，汰虛冗，益廉俸，選書吏，輸漕粟，變武科，言合旨要。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the throne admonished the bureaucracy, Richang submitted six proposals: promote talent, cut dead posts, increase honest salaries, select clerks, deliver tribute grain, and reform the military examination—words that matched the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight the emperor issued a lecture to his officials; Ding answered with six reforms—recruit talent, eliminate redundant posts, raise honest stipends, improve clerical selection, secure canal grain, and overhaul military examinations—each point striking the throne's concerns.

sentences.zh: 遭憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，起授福建巡撫，兼督船政，辭，不允。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Guangxu reign he was recalled and appointed governor of Fujian, also to supervise the naval dockyard; he declined but was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year one brought recall as Fujian governor with concurrent charge of the Foochow Navy Yard. He tried to decline; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，會霪雨，城內水逾丈，躬散賑，口煦手拊，卵翼備至，全濟災民數十萬。

translations.literal: Once he took up his duties, torrential rains flooded the city to more than ten feet; he personally distributed relief, speaking gently and comforting with his hands, nurturing the victims as a hen broods chicks, and fully saved several hundred thousand sufferers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he assumed office, weeks of rain put more than ten feet of water inside the city walls. He went out himself to distribute relief, speaking softly and laying hands on the afflicted with almost maternal care, and kept several hundred thousand people alive.

sentences.zh: 眾感泣，僉曰：「活我者，丁中丞也！」

translations.literal: The crowd wept and all said: "The one who saved us is Vice-Governor Ding!"
translations.idiomatic: People wept with gratitude and said as one, "Vice-Governor Ding is the man who saved our lives!"

sentences.zh: 時台灣生番未靖，遂力疾渡台，自北而南，所至扶服蟻伏。

translations.literal: At that time the raw tribes of Taiwan were not yet pacified, so he forced himself, though ill, to cross to Taiwan; from north to south wherever he went they submitted like ants.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan's indigenous peoples were still unsettled, so despite illness he crossed the strait. Moving from north to south, he brought district after district to submission.

sentences.zh: 惟鳳山轄境，悉芒社及獅頭、龜紋諸社素梗化，遣兵討平之，為立善後章程，皆遵約束。

translations.literal: Only in the jurisdiction of Fengshan, where the Mangshe and the Shitou and Guiwen communities had long resisted civilization, did he send troops to subdue them, establish follow-up regulations, and bring all under discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Fengshan, where the Mangshe and the Lion's Head and Tortoise-Pattern communities had long defied Qing rule, did he need force. Once pacified, he set lasting regulations and kept every village under discipline.

sentences.zh: 中路水埔六社不諳樹藝，僱漢民代耕，謂之「租坰」。

translations.literal: The six Shuipu communities of the central route did not know farming; he hired Han Chinese to farm for them, calling this "rented fields."
translations.idiomatic: Six Shuipu villages in the interior knew nothing of agriculture; he hired Han tenants to till their land under the arrangement called "rented fields."

sentences.zh: 復令有司計口給銀米，教之耕作；

translations.literal: He further ordered local officials to ration silver and grain by head count and teach them cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He told local officials to issue silver and grain by household and teach the people how to farm.

sentences.zh: 廣設義學，教之識字。

translations.literal: He widely founded charity schools and taught them literacy.
translations.idiomatic: He opened charity schools across the region and taught literacy.

sentences.zh: 又罷台屬漁戶稅。

translations.literal: He also abolished the fishermen's tax in Taiwan dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the fishing tax levied on Taiwan's coastal households.

sentences.zh: 擬築鐵路，開礦產，移關稅釐榷造船械，台民​​漸喁喁望治矣。

translations.literal: He planned railways, opened mines, shifted customs and likin revenue to fund shipbuilding, and the people of Taiwan gradually looked to good government with eager hope.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted plans for railways and mines, redirected customs and likin receipts to naval construction, and the Taiwanese began to look to his administration with rising hope.

sentences.zh: 還閩，移疾去，吏民啼泣遮道。

translations.literal: Returning to Fujian, he resigned on grounds of illness; officials and people wept and blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Fujian and resigned citing illness, magistrates and commoners alike wept and barred his carriage from leaving.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾稍間，被命赴福州，理烏石山教案。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when his illness eased somewhat, he was ordered to go to Fuzhou to handle the Wushishan missionary case.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, as his health improved slightly, the court ordered him to Fuzhou to settle the Black Rock Hill missionary affair.

sentences.zh: 先是道光間，英人就山築室傳教，疆吏不能爭，以山在城外，飾詞入告。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Daoguang era, Englishmen had built houses on the hill to preach; border officials could not contest it and reported falsely that the hill lay outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang, British missionaries had built on the hill; provincial officials, unable to resist, told Beijing the site lay outside the city—an outright fiction.

sentences.zh: 厥後佔地愈廣，閩人忿，幾釀變。

translations.literal: Afterward their occupied land grew wider; Fujianese grew angry and nearly provoked an uprising.
translations.idiomatic: The mission's footprint kept expanding; Fujianese anger mounted and violence nearly broke out.

sentences.zh: 日昌撫閩，與力爭，議易以城外電局空地。

translations.literal: When Richang governed Fujian he struggled hard and proposed exchanging the site for vacant land by the telegraph office outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian governor, Ding fought the encroachment and proposed swapping the hill for open ground near the telegraph bureau outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 未及行，遽解職，英人佔如故。

translations.literal: Before this could be carried out he was abruptly removed; the English occupation continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before the exchange could take effect he was suddenly dismissed, and British occupation continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 閩人不能忍，聚眾毀教堂，英使責難亟，至是命日昌往按。

translations.literal: The Fujianese could not endure it, gathered and destroyed the church, the English minister pressed hard, and at this point Richang was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Fujianese patience snapped; a mob wrecked the church. London protested fiercely, and the court now sent Ding to investigate.

sentences.zh: 鉤稽舊案，獲教士侵地左證，與英領事往復詰辯，卒徙教堂城外，閩人鑱石刊績焉。

translations.literal: He traced the old records, obtained proof of the missionaries' encroachment, argued back and forth with the British consul, and finally moved the church outside the city; the Fujianese carved stone to record his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Ding combed the archives, secured evidence of missionary land-grabs, debated the British consul point by point, and at last relocated the church beyond the walls. Grateful Fujianese cut stone to commemorate the deed.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，還裡。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he went home.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔加總督銜，令駐南洋會辦海防，水師統歸節度。

translations.literal: The next year an edict added the rank of governor-general and ordered him to station at Nanyang to jointly manage coastal defense, with all naval forces under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the throne gave him governor-general rank and stationed him in the south to coordinate coastal defense, placing the entire fleet under his direction.

sentences.zh: 復命充兼理各國事務大臣，以疾辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to serve concurrently as Minister for Foreign Affairs; he pleaded illness but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named concurrent Minister of Foreign Affairs; he begged off on grounds of illness, but the court would not release him.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; mourning rites followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year eight; the court granted the prescribed mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 日昌性孝友，撫吳日，母黃年九十矣，迎養署中，孺慕如兒時。

translations.literal: Richang was filial and brotherly by nature; while governing Wu, his mother Huang was already ninety; he brought her to the yamen to support her, doting on her as in childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was devoted to family. While governing Jiangsu, he brought his ninety-year-old mother Huang into the yamen and cared for her with a child's tenderness.

sentences.zh: 兄寢疾，藥饍躬侍，兄止之，則引李勣焚須事為喻。

translations.literal: When his elder brother lay ill he personally attended with medicine and food; when his brother stopped him he cited Li Ji's burning his beard as an example.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother fell ill he personally prepared medicine and meals. His brother protested; Ding answered by citing how Li Ji once burned his beard to cure his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 好藏書，成持靜齋書目五卷，世比之范氏天一閣、黃氏百宋一廛雲。

translations.literal: He loved collecting books, compiled the five-volume Catalogue of the Chijing Studio, and the world compared it to Fan's Tianyi Pavilion and Huang's Hundred Song Studio.
translations.idiomatic: A passionate bibliophile, he compiled the five-volume catalogue of his Chijing Studio collection, which contemporaries ranked beside Fan Qin's Tianyi Pavilion and Huang Pilie's Hundred Song Studio.

sentences.zh: 子五人，惠康最著，好學，多泛覽，有丁徵君遺集。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Huikang was the most noted, fond of learning and wide reading, and left the Collected Works of Mr. Ding the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Of his five sons, Huikang was best known—a wide reader who left the Collected Works of Mr. Ding the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 卞寶第，字頌臣，江蘇儀徵人。

translations.literal: Bian Baodi, style name Songchen, was a native of Yizheng, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Baodi, courtesy name Songchen, came from Yizheng in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the first year of the Xianfeng reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in Xianfeng year one.

sentences.zh: 入貲為刑部主事，累遷郎中、浙江道監察御史。

translations.literal: He purchased entry as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments and was promoted through vice-director to supervising censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way into the Ministry of Punishments as a principal secretary, rose to vice-director, and became a supervising censor on the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 軍興，官吏多避罪冒功，奏請檢視各省兵糧數目、攻守要害，及失陷收復時日功罪，以資稽覈；

translations.literal: With war rising, many officials evaded blame and claimed merit falsely; he memorialized to inspect each province's troop and grain figures, strategic points for attack and defense, and the dates of loss, recovery, merit, and guilt for verification.
translations.idiomatic: As war spread, officials often dodged blame while inflating merit. He asked the throne to audit each province's troop rolls, grain stores, strategic points, and the exact dates of defeats and recoveries so rewards and punishments could be checked.

sentences.zh: 其有獲罪之員，藉事開復保升，宜嚴定限制。

translations.literal: For those who had been punished but used events to secure restoration and promotion, strict limits should be set.
translations.idiomatic: Men already punished who used fresh incidents to win reinstatement or promotion, he said, must face tighter limits.

sentences.zh: 又言：「苗沛霖、王來鳳乍服乍叛，宜專意主剿。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Miao Peilin and Wang Laifeng submit and rebel by turns; the court should focus on extermination."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged: "Miao Peilin and Wang Laifeng sway between surrender and revolt—the policy must be extermination, not appeasement."

sentences.zh: 上皆韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor endorsed every point.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，遷禮科給事中，劾江北水師總統黃彬侵釐通賊，督辦軍務侍郎勝保貪蹇，提督成明擁兵同州畏葸無戰志，一時推為敢言。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he was moved to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Rites and impeached Huang Bin, president of the northern naval forces on the Yangtze, for embezzling likin and colluding with bandits; Vice Minister Sheng Bao for greed and obstruction; and Commander Cheng Ming for holding troops at Tongzhou in cowardice without will to fight—at the time he was praised as outspoken.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi year one brought promotion to supervising secretary of rites. He impeached Huang Bin, Yangtze naval commander, for stealing likin and aiding rebels; Grand Secretary Sheng Bao for greed and obstruction; and General Cheng Ming for hoarding troops at Tongzhou without fighting spirit. He was hailed as a fearless censor.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府府丞，遷府尹，捕巨盜王景漋等。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, then prefect, and captured the great bandit Wang Jingzhan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice prefect and then prefect of Shuntian, he captured the bandit chieftain Wang Jingzhan and his gang.

sentences.zh: 五年，乞開缺養親，不允。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he begged leave to nurse his parents; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he asked to resign and care for his parents; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 出為河南布政使，擢福建巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as provincial treasurer of Henan and was promoted to governor of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as Henan treasurer and was soon made Fujian governor.

sentences.zh: 時粵寇初平，游勇土匪肆掠，疏請就地正法，報可。

translations.literal: When the Guangdong rebels had just been pacified, roaming soldiers and bandits plundered freely; he memorialized for summary execution on the spot, which was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebellion had barely ended in the south; demobilized troops and bandits looted at will. He secured imperial approval to execute the worst offenders locally without delay.

sentences.zh: 九年，再乞終養，許之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again begged to retire and care for his parents until their death; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he again asked to retire and nurse his parents to the end; this time the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，起湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of the Guangxu reign he was recalled as governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year eight recalled him as Hunan governor.

sentences.zh: 平江方雪璈，龍陽曹小湖，安鄉周萬益、張景來，皆盜魁也，陰結徒黨，號「哥老會」。

translations.literal: Fang Xueyao of Pingjiang, Cao Xiaohu of Longyang, Zhou Wanyi and Zhang Jinglai of Anxiang were all bandit chiefs who secretly formed gangs calling themselves the "Gelaohui."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xueyao of Pingjiang, Cao Xiaohu of Longyang, and Zhou Wanyi and Zhang Jinglai of Anxiang were bandit leaders who formed secret societies calling themselves the Elder Brothers.

sentences.zh: 寶第悉置之法。

translations.literal: Baodi had them all executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Bian had every one of them executed.

sentences.zh: 署湖廣總督。

translations.literal: He served as acting governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He acted as governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 法人侵越南，詔偕巡撫彭祖賢治江防，築砲台田家鎮南北岸各三座，繪具圖說上之。

translations.literal: When the French invaded Vietnam, an edict ordered him together with Governor Peng Zuxian to manage Yangtze defenses; he built three batteries on each bank at Tianjiazhen and submitted illustrated reports.
translations.idiomatic: When France invaded Vietnam, he and Hunan governor Peng Zuxian were ordered to strengthen Yangtze defenses. Bian built three gun platforms on each bank at Tianjiazhen and sent illustrated plans to the court.

sentences.zh: 時議建樊口石閘。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of building a stone sluice at Fankou.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were debating a stone floodgate at Fankou.

sentences.zh: 寶第以謂：「樊口內有梁子諸湖，袤延八百里，水皆無源，江入其中，瀦為巨浸。

translations.literal: Baodi said: "Within Fankou are the Liangzi lakes, stretching eight hundred li; their waters have no source, and when the Yangtze enters them it becomes a vast flood.
translations.idiomatic: Bian argued: "Inside Fankou lie the Liangzi lakes, eight hundred li across. They have no independent source; when the Yangtze pours in, the whole basin becomes a vast inland sea.

sentences.zh: 以民情論，重在堵江水之入，不在洩內水之出。

translations.literal: From the people's situation, the emphasis should be on blocking Yangtze water from entering, not on draining inner water outward.
translations.idiomatic: For the people, the priority is keeping river water out, not draining lake water out.

sentences.zh: 以地勢論，江水驟失此渟瀦八百里地，則下游堤防必致衝決。

translations.literal: From the terrain, if the Yangtze suddenly lost this eight-hundred-li storage, downstream dikes would surely burst.
translations.idiomatic: Geographically, if the river suddenly lost eight hundred li of storage, levees downstream would certainly fail.

sentences.zh: 請緩建石閘，而漸除樊口內窪田額賦。」

translations.literal: He asked to delay building the stone sluice and gradually remove the land-tax quota on low fields within Fankou."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to postpone the stone sluice and gradually lift land-tax quotas on flooded fields inside Fankou."

sentences.zh: 得旨允行。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，還湖南巡撫任。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he returned to his post as governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he resumed the Hunan governorship.

sentences.zh: 法人款成，寶第上言：「各國通商，因利乘便，須具臥薪嘗膽之志，為苞桑陰雨之謀。」

translations.literal: After peace with France, Baodi memorialized: "When all nations trade, they seize advantage; we must have the resolve of sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, and make plans as for storm and rain on the mulberry."
translations.idiomatic: After the French treaty, Bian wrote: "Foreign trade lets every power take advantage; we need the resolve of King Goujian—sleeping on brushwood, tasting gall—and plans as if disaster were always one season away."

sentences.zh: 因條上求才、裕餉、船政、器械四事。

translations.literal: He then listed four items: seeking talent, securing revenue, naval administration, and arms.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with four programs: talent, revenue, shipbuilding, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 又言：「國家財用，歲出大宗，莫如兵勇並設。

translations.literal: He also said: "Of the state's annual expenditures, the largest item is maintaining both regular troops and braves together.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Among state expenditures, nothing matches the cost of keeping both Green Standard troops and volunteer braves on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 直省旗綠各營兵額七十七萬，每年薪糧銀一千數百萬兩。

translations.literal: In all provinces the banner and Green Standard quotas total 770,000 men, with annual pay and grain silver of more than ten million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial banner and Green Standard establishments list 770,000 men and consume more than ten million taels a year in pay and grain.

sentences.zh: 養兵既多，費餉尤巨。

translations.literal: With so many soldiers maintained, the cost of pay is especially huge.
translations.idiomatic: So many men on payroll make the ration bill enormous.

sentences.zh: 兵多則力弱，餉巨則國貧。

translations.literal: Many soldiers mean weak force; huge pay means a poor state.
translations.idiomatic: Mass armies weaken fighting power; massive pay drains the treasury.

sentences.zh: 粵逆初起金田，僅二千人。

translations.literal: The Guangdong rebels first rose at Jintian with only two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping began at Jintian with barely two thousand fighters.

sentences.zh: 廣西額兵二萬三千，土兵一萬四千。

translations.literal: Guangxi had 23,000 quota troops and 14,000 local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi fielded 23,000 regulars and 14,000 local militia.

sentences.zh: 乃以三萬七千之兵，不能擊二千之賊，廣西兵不可用，他省可推。

translations.literal: Yet 37,000 troops could not strike 2,000 rebels; Guangxi troops were useless, and other provinces could be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: Yet 37,000 soldiers could not defeat 2,000 rebels. If Guangxi's army was useless, other provinces were no better.

sentences.zh: 其後發、捻、田、苗等匪，悉賴湘、淮營勇勘定，綠營戰績無聞。

translations.literal: Afterward the Fa, Nian, Tian, and Miao bandits were all suppressed by Hunan and Huai braves; the Green Standard had no battle record to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Taiping, Nian, Tian, and Miao rebellions were crushed by Hunan and Huai volunteer corps; the Green Standard won no fame in battle.

sentences.zh: 大亂甫夷，伏莽未盡，兵不得力，勇難驟撤，於是歲支勇糧一千餘萬。

translations.literal: Great disorder had just ended and hidden trouble was not exhausted; regular troops were ineffective and braves could not be suddenly disbanded, so annual brave rations exceeded ten million.
translations.idiomatic: The great rebellions had barely ended and bandits still lurked; regulars were useless and braves could not be disbanded overnight, so brave rations alone exceeded ten million taels yearly.

sentences.zh: 賦入有常，豈能堪此耗費？

translations.literal: Revenue has fixed limits—how can it bear such waste?
translations.idiomatic: Tax income is fixed—how can the state sustain such waste?

sentences.zh: 查綠營馬兵每月一兩九錢，戰兵一兩四錢，守兵九錢零。

translations.literal: Green Standard cavalry receive one tael nine mace monthly, combat soldiers one tael four mace, garrison soldiers nine mace odd.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard cavalry receive 1.9 taels a month, combat soldiers 1.4, garrison troops barely 0.9.

sentences.zh: 月餼無多，必謀別業，遂弛專操，軍情瞬變，調發遷延。

translations.literal: With so little monthly ration they must seek other livelihood, so drill is neglected; military readiness changes in an instant and mobilization is delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Pay so low forces other trades; drill slackens; armies that should move at once arrive late.

sentences.zh: 臣擬請裁額並糧，以兩額挑養一兵。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes to cut quotas and combine rations, using two quotas to support one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: I propose cutting nominal rolls and merging pay so two paper slots fund one real soldier.

sentences.zh: 如額兵一萬，半為駐守，半赴巡防，互相邏戍，共習辛勤，常則計日操演，變則隨時援應。

translations.literal: If quota troops number ten thousand, half garrison and half patrol, rotating duty, sharing hardship, drilling daily in peace and responding when crisis comes.
translations.idiomatic: Take ten thousand men on paper: half garrison, half patrol, rotating posts, training daily in peace, responding instantly in crisis.

sentences.zh: 副參任營官，都守充哨弁，室家無累，而後紀律可嚴。

translations.literal: Deputy generals serve as camp officers, colonels as squad leaders; without family burdens discipline can be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Let deputy generals command camps and colonels lead squads; men without families at their heels can be held to strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 此宜變通營製者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first matter in which camp organization should be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first reform the camp system needs.

sentences.zh: 兵擬減額，原設將弁亦應核減。

translations.literal: If troop quotas are to be cut, the original officers should also be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: If soldier quotas shrink, officer posts must shrink too.

sentences.zh: 綠營將弁歲領廉俸雜項，職大者可抵百兵數十兵，小者亦抵十餘兵。

translations.literal: Green Standard officers yearly receive stipends and extras; the highest equal dozens or hundreds of soldiers, the lowest more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard officers draw stipends worth dozens of soldiers' pay at the top ranks and more than ten at the bottom.

sentences.zh: 自來積弊，隱匿空糧，攤扣月餉，左右役使，無非額兵。

translations.literal: Long-standing abuses hide empty quotas, deduct monthly pay, and use quota soldiers as personal servants.
translations.idiomatic: Long abuse hides phantom rolls, skims monthly pay, and turns nominal soldiers into officers' servants.

sentences.zh: 裁汰之議，自非將弁所樂。

translations.literal: Talk of cutting is naturally not what officers welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Officers naturally hate talk of cuts.

sentences.zh: 擬請先裁將弁以並營，營兵必多，乃漸裁兵，老弱事故缺出停補，俟空千名，即補精壯五百，綠營不足，簡撥營勇，作為練軍。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes first to cut officers and merge camps; with more soldiers per camp, then gradually cut soldiers; stop filling vacancies for the old and weak until a thousand gaps appear, then fill five hundred with strong men; where Green Standard is insufficient, select braves as drill troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cut officers first and merge camps; when each camp holds more real men, thin the rolls; stop replacing dead or aged men until a thousand slots are empty, then fill five hundred with the strong; where Green Standard fails, draft braves into drill corps.

sentences.zh: 不啟兵眾之疑，自無阻撓之慮。

translations.literal: Without arousing soldiers' suspicion, there will be no fear of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Done this way, troops will not suspect a purge and resistance will fade.

sentences.zh: 此宜逐漸辦理者又一也。

translations.literal: This is the second matter to be handled gradually.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second reform to phase in slowly.

sentences.zh: 目前兵尚未練，勇已議裁，若欲節餉，則裁勇不足資緩急，裁兵為有備而無患。」

translations.literal: At present troops are not yet drilled and braves are already slated for cuts; if savings are wanted, cutting braves cannot meet emergencies while cutting regulars keeps readiness without peril."
translations.idiomatic: Today regulars are untrained while braves face cuts. To save money, cutting braves leaves no reserve; cutting regulars keeps defense without disaster."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢閩浙總督，兼管福建船政。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang, also managing the Fujian naval dockyard.
translations.idiomatic: Year fourteen made him governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang with charge of the Foochow Navy Yard.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以疾解職，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he resigned on illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen he resigned for illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 寶第有威重，不為小謹，騶從甚盛，所至誅鋤奸猾，扶槙良願，民尤感之。

translations.literal: Baodi had imposing authority, did not fuss over small proprieties, and traveled with a large retinue; wherever he went he executed the crafty and supported the honest and willing, and the people were especially grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Bian carried weight and scorned petty etiquette, traveling with a large escort. Everywhere he executed rascals and backed honest folk, and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 子緒昌，戶部七品小京官。

translations.literal: His son Xuchang was a seventh-rank secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuchang served as a seventh-rank secretary in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 塗宗瀛，號朗軒，安徽六安人。

translations.literal: Tu Zongying, style name Langxuan, was a native of Lu'an, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Zongying, known as Langxuan, came from Lu'an in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以舉人銓江蘇知縣。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he was selected as Jiangsu magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the provincial exams he was appointed a Jiangsu county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓督兩江，檄主軍糈，累保授江寧知府。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan governed the two Jiang circuits, he was ordered to manage army provisions and through repeated recommendations was appointed prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan governed Jiangnan, Tu was ordered to manage army grain and, on repeated recommendation, became prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 同治九年，擢蘇松太道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Tongzhi reign he was promoted to Intendant of Su-Song-Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi year nine raised him to intendant of the Suzhou–Songjiang–Taicang circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷湖南按察使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to judicial commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Hunan's judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 湘民故健訟，都察院歲所下獄輒逾百數。

translations.literal: Hunan people were fond of litigation; each year the Censorate sent more than a hundred cases to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Hunanese were famously litigious; the Censorate each year forwarded more than a hundred cases to jail.

sentences.zh: 宗瀛為立條教，允首悔，懲誣告，並嚴定審理功過章程，弊乃稍革。

translations.literal: Zongying established regulations, allowed first repentance, punished false accusation, and strictly fixed merit-and-fault rules for trials, so abuses were somewhat reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Tu set rules allowing first offenders to repent, punished false accusers, and tied magistrates' performance reviews to fair trials, and the worst abuses eased.

sentences.zh: 晉布政使，仿硃子社倉法，建立長沙府倉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial treasurer and, following Zhu Xi's community-granary method, established the Changsha prefectural granary.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to treasurer, he modeled Zhu Xi's community granary system and built the Changsha prefectural storehouse.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，拜廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Guangxu reign he was appointed governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year three made him Guangxi governor.

sentences.zh: 苗、瑤、倮儸獷悍梗化，檄所屬廣建學塾，刊孝經、小學諸書，使之誦習；

translations.literal: The Miao, Yao, and Lolo were fierce and resisted civilization; he ordered subordinates to build many schools, print the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning and have them recited.
translations.idiomatic: Miao, Yao, and Lolo peoples were fierce and defied assimilation; he ordered schools built everywhere, printed the Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning, and required recitation.

sentences.zh: 又自撰歌詞以勸戒之。

translations.literal: He also composed songs himself to admonish them.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote moral songs of his own to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 時晉、豫大旱，移撫河南，割取俸餘萬二千金助賑，招流亡，給籽種，老穉無依者，設廠收養，強有力者任工作。

translations.literal: When Shanxi and Henan suffered great drought, he was moved to govern Henan, cut twelve thousand taels from his salary for relief, gathered the displaced, gave seed, set shelters for the old and young without support, and put the strong to work.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Shanxi and Henan, he was transferred to Henan, donated twelve thousand taels of salary for relief, resettled refugees, distributed seed, sheltered the helpless, and put able-bodied men to work.

sentences.zh: 世與曾國荃賑晉並稱雲。

translations.literal: The world paired his name with Zeng Guoquan's Shanxi relief.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries ranked his Henan relief beside Zeng Guoquan's work in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 七年，調湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he returned as Hunan governor.

sentences.zh: 撫標兵譁變，懲四人而事定。

translations.literal: The provincial garrison mutinied; he punished four men and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial banner troops mutinied, he executed four ringleaders and order returned.

sentences.zh: 及擢總督，又有武漢教匪之亂，捕誅數十人，亦遂安堵。

translations.literal: After promotion to governor-general, there was also the Wuhan sectarian uprising; he captured and executed several dozen and peace was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After he became governor-general, Wuhan's sectarian rebels rose; he captured and executed dozens, and the city calmed.

sentences.zh: 言官先後糾彈，事下彭玉麟，坐才力竭蹶，纟圭吏議。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him in succession; the case went to Peng Yulin, who found his talent exhausted and imposed demerit on the official record.
translations.idiomatic: Censors repeatedly impeached him; Peng Yulin investigated, judged his strength spent, and recorded a demerit against him.

sentences.zh: 無何，御史陳啟泰劾宗瀛務封殖，仍下玉麟按覆，玉麟後白其誣。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Chen Qitai impeached Zongying for self-enrichment; the case again went to Yulin for review, and Yulin later cleared him of false charge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Censor Chen Qitai accused Tu of hoarding wealth; Peng Yulin reviewed the case again and eventually cleared him.

sentences.zh: 時左宗棠督江南，欲規复淮鹽、減川引，宗瀛以減川增淮，關川省數十萬鹽丁運夫生計，因抗疏力爭，言：「按年減運，則未運者將盡化為私。

translations.literal: At the time Zuo Zongtang governed Jiangnan and wished to restore Huai salt and reduce Sichuan quota; Zongying held that reducing Sichuan to increase Huai concerned the livelihood of hundreds of thousands of Sichuan salt workers and carriers, and memorialized in strong opposition, saying: "If transport is reduced year by year, what is not transported will all turn private.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang then governed Jiangnan and wanted to restore Huai salt at Sichuan's expense. Tu argued that shifting quota would ruin hundreds of thousands of Sichuan salt workers and carriers, and memorialized fiercely: "Annual cuts in legal transport will simply turn the remainder into smuggling.

sentences.zh: 縱使湖北置兵徼循，而巫峽流急，鹽船下駛，瞬息百里，兵少力不能制，多恐滋生事端。

translations.literal: Even if Hubei posts troops to patrol, the Wu Gorge current is swift and salt boats downstream run a hundred li in an instant; few troops cannot control it and trouble will easily arise.
translations.idiomatic: Even with Hubei patrols, the Wu Gorge current sweeps salt boats a hundred li in minutes—too few troops to control, and violence would follow.

sentences.zh: 且鄂餉無著，下拂輿情，上虧國帑。」

translations.literal: Moreover Hubei revenue would have no source, popular feeling below would be offended, and the national treasury above would lose."
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's revenue would collapse, public anger would rise, and the treasury would lose."

sentences.zh: 辭愷切。

translations.literal: His words were earnest and moving.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was passionate and persuasive.

sentences.zh: 未幾，稱疾乞休歸。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded illness and retired home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned citing illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 初，宗瀛從廷棟講學，為刊遺集，以理學稱。

translations.literal: Earlier Zongying had studied under Ting Dong and published his posthumous works, and was known for Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in life Tu had studied under Ting Dong, published his teacher's works, and was known as a Neo-Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 家居十餘載，以徐延旭獲譴，追坐舉主，下部察議。

translations.literal: After more than ten years at home, because Xu Yanxu was punished, he was traced as recommender and the ministries deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: After a decade in retirement, Xu Yanxu's disgrace implicated Tu as his patron, and the ministries opened an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died at age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year twenty at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 黎培敬，字簡堂，湖南湘潭人。

translations.literal: Li Peijing, style name Jiantang, was a native of Xiangtan, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Peijing, courtesy name Jiantang, came from Xiangtan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the tenth year of Xianfeng, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Xianfeng year ten, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，出督貴州學政。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi he went out as educational commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi year three sent him as Guizhou education commissioner.

sentences.zh: 阻寇弗能進，乃從劉岳昭借軍數十，竟達貴陽。

translations.literal: Blocked by bandits he could not advance, so he borrowed several dozen troops from Liu Yuezhao and finally reached Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits blocked his route; he borrowed dozens of soldiers from Liu Yuezhao and at last reached Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 時總督勞崇光、巡撫張亮基不相協，軍事益壞。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General Lao Chongguang and Governor Zhang Liangji did not cooperate and military affairs grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lao Chongguang and Governor Zhang Liangji feuded, and the military situation worsened.

sentences.zh: 培敬上書言狀，朝廷始獲聞邊事。

translations.literal: Peijing wrote describing the situation and the court first learned of border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li wrote frankly about conditions, and Beijing first learned the truth about the border.

sentences.zh: 黔苗俶擾，謳誦寂寥。

translations.literal: The Qian Miao were in sudden turmoil and praise and song were silent.
translations.idiomatic: Miao unrest had silenced scholarship and public morale in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 培敬曰：「士氣不伸，人心所繇不靖也。」

translations.literal: Peijing said: "When scholar spirit is not extended, the people's hearts are thereby unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "When scholars' morale collapses, the people's hearts cannot stay calm."

sentences.zh: 於是出入寇氛，按試州縣，雖危棘不緩期，貴州士民始復知文教。

translations.literal: He then went in and out of bandit atmosphere, conducted examinations in prefectures and counties, and though in peril did not delay schedule; Guizhou scholars and people first again knew civilization and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He toured districts even amid banditry, held examinations on schedule despite danger, and slowly restored Guizhou's faith in education.

sentences.zh: 道黔西，晤道員岑毓英，與語，知其諳戎事，遂請以滇中軍屬之。

translations.literal: Passing western Guizhou he met Circuit Intendant Cen Yuying; in conversation he knew him versed in military affairs and requested that Yunnan troops be placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In western Guizhou he met Circuit Intendant Cen Yuying, recognized a military mind, and asked that Yunnan forces be placed under him.

sentences.zh: 培敬秩滿，以太常寺卿石贊清薦，命權布政使。

translations.literal: When Peijing's term ended, on recommendation of Minister of Rites Shi Zanqing he was ordered to act as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, Minister of Rites Shi Zanqing recommended him to act as provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 其時寇患方亟，賊酋潘名桀守龍里，久不下。

translations.literal: At that time bandit trouble was acute; bandit chief Pan Mingjie held Longli and long could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was acute; chieftain Pan Mingjie held Longli and would not fall.

sentences.zh: 培敬曰：「今附郭百里，倉廩猶實。

translations.literal: Peijing said: "Within a hundred li of the city, granaries are still full.
translations.idiomatic: Li warned, "Within a hundred li of the capital, granaries are still full.

sentences.zh: 不因以為資，若轉藉寇，吾屬必為所虜矣！」

translations.literal: If we do not use this as resource, but instead rely on bandits, we shall surely be captured by them!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to use that grain and instead feed the rebels, we ourselves will be their captives!"

sentences.zh: 因說提督出城取龍里，逾歲，克之。

translations.literal: He therefore persuaded the commander to leave the city and take Longli; after more than a year it was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He persuaded the commander to march out, take Longli, and after a year the city fell.

sentences.zh: 旋复貴定，名桀遁去，黔軍克捷自此始。

translations.literal: Soon Guiyang was recovered, Mingjie fled, and from this the Qian army's victories began.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang was recovered, Pan Mingjie fled, and Guizhou's counteroffensive began.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之，予實授。

translations.literal: An edict praised him and granted substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised him and confirmed his appointment.

sentences.zh: 繇是東定都勻，北靖開、修，南平陳喬生，西除林自清，蒞黔數載，境內悉平。

translations.literal: Thereafter he pacified east at Duyun, north at Kai and Xiu, south at Chen Qiaosheng, west at Lin Ziqing; governing Qian several years, the whole territory was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified Duyun in the east, Kai and Xiu in the north, Chen Qiaosheng in the south, and Lin Ziqing in the west; within years all Guizhou was calm.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: At the change to Guangxu he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the Guangxu succession he became governor.

sentences.zh: 繼曾璧光後，益嚴吏治。

translations.literal: Following Zeng Biguang he tightened official discipline still more.
translations.idiomatic: After Zeng Biguang he tightened official discipline further.

sentences.zh: 以上疏請釋前總督賀長齡處分並予諡建祠，鐫秩罷歸。

translations.literal: Because he memorialized to release former Governor-General He Changling's punishment and grant posthumous title and temple, he was demoted in rank and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore former governor-general He Changling and build him a temple; the court demoted him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 五年，起四川按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled as judicial commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Year five recalled him as Sichuan judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時丁寶楨督蜀，課吏嚴。

translations.literal: At the time Ding Baozhen governed Shu and was strict in assessing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Baozhen governed Sichuan with stern discipline toward officials.

sentences.zh: 培敬至，寶楨出郊迎，曰：「此吾貴州賢使君也！」

translations.literal: When Peijing arrived, Baozhen went to the suburbs to welcome him, saying: "This is my worthy commissioner from Guizhou!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li arrived, Ding met him outside the city, saying, "Here is my worthy commissioner from Guizhou!"

sentences.zh: 培敬以巡撫降官，絕無慍意，孜孜治事。

translations.literal: Peijing had been demoted from governor but had no resentment and worked diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Though demoted from governor, Li showed no resentment and worked tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 寶楨數薦其賢。

translations.literal: Baozhen repeatedly recommended his worth.
translations.idiomatic: Ding repeatedly recommended his talent.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Year six made him Director-General of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 漕督雖閒職，然膴仕，培敬誓不以自污，公費所餘，以之修驛館，建兵房，增書院餐錢，興釋奠禮器，官煤、利濟諸局亦賡續告成，人無敢干以私。

translations.literal: Though the grain transport post was leisurely, it was a lucrative office; Peijing vowed not to stain himself, and used surplus public funds to repair post stations, build barracks, increase academy stipends, restore sacrificial vessels, and complete the official coal and Liji bureaus; no one dared approach him for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: The grain transport post was prestigious and lucrative, but Li refused to soil his hands. Surplus funds went to post roads, barracks, academy stipends, ritual vessels, and the official coal and charity bureaus; no one dared solicit private favors.

sentences.zh: 七年，授江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven appointed him Jiangsu governor.

sentences.zh: 未上，疾作，遂告歸。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post illness came and he resigned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, illness forced retirement.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，優詔賜卹，諡文肅，予貴陽、清江浦建祠。

translations.literal: The next year he died; an excellent edict granted mourning honors, posthumous title Wensu, and temples at Guiyang and Qingjiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year; the court granted lavish mourning, posthumous title Wensu, and temples at Guiyang and Qingjiangpu.

sentences.zh: 崧駿，字鎮青，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。

translations.literal: Song Jun, style name Zhenqing, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Bannerman of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jun, courtesy name Zhenqing, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年舉人，由兵部筆帖式累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the eighth year of Xianfeng and rose from a clerk in the Ministry of War to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed provincial exams in Xianfeng year eight and rose from War Ministry clerk to director.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，出知廣東高州府，以憂解。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi he went out as prefect of Gaozhou, Guangdong, and left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi year six made him Gaozhou prefect in Guangdong; he left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，起授山東沂州府，歷廣西按察使、直隸布政使、漕運總督。

translations.literal: After mourning he was appointed Yizhou prefect in Shandong, then served as Guangxi judicial commissioner, Zhili treasurer, and Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as Yizhou prefect in Shandong, then Guangxi judicial commissioner, Zhili treasurer, and grain transport director-general.

sentences.zh: 光緒十二年，巡撫江蘇，調浙江，所至興利除弊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Guangxu he governed Jiangsu, then was transferred to Zhejiang; wherever he went he promoted benefit and removed harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year twelve made him Jiangsu governor, then Zhejiang governor; everywhere he sought public good.

sentences.zh: 以南糧改折色，吏民交困，並減旗營民糧、織造匠糧，令州縣糶價以供漕，弊乃革。

translations.literal: Because southern grain was changed to cash payment, officials and people were both distressed; he also reduced banner and artisan grain quotas and ordered prefectures and counties to sell grain at market price for tribute transport, and abuses were reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Converting southern grain tribute to cash had squeezed officials and people alike. He cut banner and artisan grain quotas and required counties to sell grain at market rates for transport, ending the worst abuses.

sentences.zh: 十五年，浙患水祲，奏請免漕，發帑賑之，而於京、協諸餉仍從容籌解，复集貲購米實倉儲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhejiang suffered flood; he memorialized to exempt tribute grain, issued treasury funds for relief, yet still calmly raised Beijing and cooperative payments, and also collected funds to buy grain to fill granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Year fifteen brought Zhejiang floods; he exempted tribute grain, opened treasury relief, still met Beijing and cooperative payments, and bought grain to refill granaries.

sentences.zh: 杭、嘉、湖三府暨蘇、松、常、太諸水源出於潛天目山附近，苕溪南北二湖為分洩地，歲久淤塞，用工賑法，招集流民疏濬之。

translations.literal: The waters of Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou and Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Taicang all rise near Qian and Tianmu mountains; the north and south Tiaoxi lakes are discharge areas but had long silted; he used work-for-relief to gather displaced people to dredge them.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Taicang all draw water from the Tianmu range; the north and south Tiaoxi lakes had silted shut. He used work-for-relief to mobilize refugees and dredge them.

sentences.zh: 其杭、嘉、湖、紹諸塘岸堰徬，靡不次第修治，民賴其利。

translations.literal: The dikes, embankments, and sluices of Hang, Jia, Hu, and Shao were all repaired in turn and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Dikes and sluices across Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Shaoxing were repaired in sequence, to the people's lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in year seventeen.

sentences.zh: 崧駿以清廉自矢，於國計民生服念不忘。

translations.literal: Song Jun held himself to integrity and never forgot national revenue and people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jun pledged himself to integrity and never forgot revenue or people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 撫江、浙績尤著，民請祠之，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: His achievements governing Jiang and Zhe were especially notable; the people requested a temple and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: His work in Jiangsu and Zhejiang was especially praised; locals won approval for a memorial temple.

sentences.zh: 子昆敬，戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Kunjing was a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kunjing served as a director in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 崧蕃，字錫侯，崧駿弟也。

translations.literal: Song Fan, style name Xihou, was the younger brother of Song Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Song Fan, courtesy name Xihou, was Song Jun's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年舉人，初入貲為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the fifth year of Xianfeng and first purchased entry as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed provincial exams in Xianfeng year five and bought his way into the Board of Personnel as a director.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，京察一等，簡四川鹽茶道，屢署按察使，保薦卓異。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he ranked first in capital inspection and was appointed Sichuan Salt Controller, repeatedly acting as judicial commissioner, and was recommended as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year five brought top capital inspection rank, appointment as Sichuan salt controller, repeated stints as judicial commissioner, and outstanding merit rating.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授湖南按察使，遷四川布政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Hunan judicial commissioner and moved to Sichuan treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Year eleven made him Hunan judicial commissioner, then Sichuan treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Year seventeen promoted him to Guizhou governor.

sentences.zh: 廣西寇陸亞漋煽亂西林，與貴州接壤，崧蕃遣將扼冊亨要隘，邊患遂平。

translations.literal: The Guangxi bandit Lu Yahuan stirred rebellion in Xilin bordering Guizhou; Song Fan sent generals to hold the Ceheng passes and the border trouble was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi rebel Lu Yahuan stirred Xilin on the Guizhou border, Song Fan sealed the Ceheng passes and ended the threat.

sentences.zh: 調雲南巡撫，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Yunnan and promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became Yunnan governor, then Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general.

sentences.zh: 檢視防營缺額積弊，劾副將雷家春，並自請議處，革職留任。

translations.literal: Inspecting long-standing abuses of vacant posts in defense camps, he impeached Deputy Commander Lei Jiachun and also asked punishment for himself, being dismissed from office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing phantom rolls in frontier garrisons, he impeached Deputy Commander Lei Jiachun, asked the court to punish himself as well, and was stripped of rank but kept at work.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，奏請陛見，值拳匪肇亂，命留京會辦城防事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he memorialized to attend audience; when the Boxer turmoil arose he was ordered to remain in the capital to manage city defense.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-six he memorialized for an audience in Beijing; when the Boxers rose he was ordered to stay and manage capital defenses.

sentences.zh: 旋扈駕至太原，飭還本任。

translations.literal: Soon he escorted the court to Taiyuan and was ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon escorted the court to Taiyuan, then was sent back to his province.

sentences.zh: 行次，調陝甘總督。

translations.literal: On the journey he was transferred to governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: En route he was transferred to Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general.

sentences.zh: 於城南建立大學堂，分兩齋，東齋考文，西齋講武。

translations.literal: At the south of the city he established a university with two halls: the east hall for literary examination, the west for military studies.
translations.idiomatic: South of the provincial city he founded a university with an east hall for classics and a west hall for military science.

sentences.zh: 而修濬寧夏七星渠，尤為民所利賴。

translations.literal: He also dredged the Ningxia Qixing Canal, which especially benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Ningxia's Qixing Canal, a boon the people long relied on.

sentences.zh: 寧郡堤工，創自乾隆時，魚鹽之利甲通省，後漸湮廢。

translations.literal: The Ning prefecture dikes were first built in the Qianlong era; the profit of fish and salt led the whole province, but later they gradually fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia's dikes dated to Qianlong, when fish and salt profits led the province, but they had decayed.

sentences.zh: 中衛縣令王樹棻素講求水利，崧蕃檄令勘工，自七星渠上接白馬通灘，流濬通深百八十餘裡，灌田六萬餘畝，磽確變為沃壤，逃亡復業。

translations.literal: Zhongwei Magistrate Wang Shufen was versed in water works; Song Fan ordered him to survey; from the Qixing Canal up to connect with Baima Tongtan, the channel was dredged more than 180 li, irrigating over 60,000 mu; barren land became fertile and the displaced returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei magistrate Wang Shufen knew hydraulics; Song ordered a survey, linked the Qixing Canal to Baima Tongtan, dredged 180 li, irrigated 60,000 mu, turned wasteland fertile, and brought refugees home.

sentences.zh: 又以渠水分自黃河，勢洶湧，春夏山水驟發，與黃流渾合，泥沙雜下，旋濬旋塞。

translations.literal: Because the canal water was drawn from the Yellow River and the current was violent, in spring and summer mountain floods suddenly came and mixed with the Yellow flow; silt came down and dredging was immediately blocked again.
translations.idiomatic: Because the canal drew Yellow River water with violent current, spring and summer floods mixed silt in and clogged the channel as fast as men cleared it.

sentences.zh: 乃仿古人暗洞激水法，凡傍山之渠，架油鬆成洞，覆以石板，山水流石上，而渠水潛行洞中。

translations.literal: He then imitated the ancient method of hidden tunnels to rush water: for canals along mountains he built tunnels of oiled pine covered with stone slabs; mountain water flowed on the stone while canal water ran hidden in the tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: He copied ancient siphon tunnels: along mountain channels he built pine-lined tunnels capped with stone so floodwater ran overhead while irrigation water ran beneath.

sentences.zh: 又度地勢築高堤，導山水使入黃河，並於渠口築進水、退水兩壩，使黃流曲折入渠，不致衝漫。

translations.literal: He also judged the terrain and built high dikes to guide mountain water into the Yellow River, and at the canal mouth built intake and discharge dams so the Yellow current entered the canal in curves and would not rush and overflow.
translations.idiomatic: He built high dikes to divert mountain floods into the Yellow River and intake and spill dams at the mouth so river water entered the canal gently.

sentences.zh: 工竣，數經暴水，卒不圮。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, though floods came several times, it never collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: After completion, repeated floods never destroyed the works.

sentences.zh: 設農務局，招墾荒地，如平羅、渭源諸縣，先後報墾數百千畝。

translations.literal: He established an agricultural bureau and recruited reclamation of wasteland; in Pingluo, Weiyuan, and other counties hundreds of thousands of mu were reported reclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He opened an agricultural bureau and sponsored reclamation; Pingluo, Weiyuan, and other counties reported hundreds of thousands of mu opened.

sentences.zh: 舊有機器局，漸次擴張。

translations.literal: The old machine works were gradually expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Existing arsenals were gradually enlarged.

sentences.zh: 凡興作實事求是，不惟其名。

translations.literal: In all undertakings he sought practical results and not mere names.
translations.idiomatic: In every project he sought results, not reputation.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，調閩浙總督，未上，以疾卒，追贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang; before taking office he died of illness and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirty-one transferred him to Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general; he died before taking office and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子外務部主事豫敬，以員外郎補用。

translations.literal: His son Yujing of the Foreign Ministry was supplemented as vice director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yujing of the Foreign Ministry was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 邊寶泉，字潤民，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Bian Baoquan, style name Runmin, was a Bannerman of the Han Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Baoquan, courtesy name Runmin, was a Han bannerman of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: He became a metropolitan graduate in the second year of Tongzhi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Tongzhi year two and became a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補浙江道監察御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed supervising censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Year eleven made him supervising censor on the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 大學士李鴻章總督直隸，奏清苑麥秀兩歧。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang, as governor-general of Zhili, memorialized that wheat in Qingyuan showed two ears on one stalk.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, governing Zhili, reported double-eared wheat in Qingyuan as an omen.

sentences.zh: 寶泉疏論之曰：「祥瑞之說，盛世不言。

translations.literal: Baoquan memorialized in rebuttal: "In an age of prosperity auspicious talk is not spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Bian memorialized in reply: "Prosperous ages do not traffic in omens.

sentences.zh: 臣來自田間，麥有兩歧，常所親見。

translations.literal: Your servant comes from the fields; wheat with two ears is commonly seen.
translations.idiomatic: I come from farming country; double-eared wheat is common.

sentences.zh: 地氣偏厚，偶然致此，何足為異？

translations.literal: When local qi is especially thick it occasionally produces this—how is it extraordinary?
translations.idiomatic: Rich soil sometimes produces it by chance—nothing miraculous.

sentences.zh: 漢章之時，以嘉穀芝草，改元章和，何敞猶據經義面折宋由、袁安。

translations.literal: In the Zhanghe era, with auspicious grain and lingzhi, the reign title was changed to Zhanghe, yet He Chang still used classical argument to rebuke Song You and Yuan An face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang of Han, lucky grain and lingzhi prompted a reign-title change, yet He Chang still rebuked flatterers Song You and Yuan An to their faces with classical argument.

sentences.zh: 至馬端臨文獻通考，乃舉歷代祥瑞，統曰'物異'。

translations.literal: When Ma Duanlin's Wenxian Tongkao lists all dynasties' auspicious signs, he groups them as 'strange things.'
translations.idiomatic: Ma Duanlin's Wenxian Tongkao lists every dynasty's omens under the heading 'strange phenomena.'

sentences.zh: 夫祥且為異，今以無異之物而謂之祥，可乎？

translations.literal: If auspicious things are still called strange, now to call unstrange things auspicious—can that stand?
translations.idiomatic: If even true omens count as oddities, how can we call an ordinary stalk auspicious?

sentences.zh: 上年畿輔水災甚鉅，迄今沒水田廬猶未盡出；

translations.literal: Last year the metropolitan region suffered great flood; submerged fields and houses are not yet all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the capital region suffered terrible floods; flooded fields and homes have not fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 永定河甫經蕆工，北岸又潰；

translations.literal: The Yongding River had just been completed, yet the north bank burst again.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongding River works had just been finished when the north bank broke again.

sentences.zh: 邊軍未撤，民困未蘇。

translations.literal: Border troops are not yet withdrawn and the people's hardship is not yet relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Border troops remain in the field and the people are still destitute.

sentences.zh: 鴻章身膺重寄，威望素隆，當效何敞之公忠，懲宋由、袁安之導媚。

translations.literal: Hongzhang bears heavy trust and has long-standing prestige; he should emulate He Chang's public loyalty and punish the flattery of Song You and Yuan An.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang holds heavy responsibility and great prestige; he should imitate He Chang's blunt loyalty and reject flatterers like Song You and Yuan An.

sentences.zh: 皇上御極之初，庶吉士嚴辰散館考試，曲意頌揚，奉旨嚴飭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's accession, Hanlin bachelor Yan Chen in the graduation examination praised obsequiously and received a stern edict.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign, Hanlin graduate Yan Chen's examination essay flattered the throne and drew a stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 今鴻章為督撫大吏，非草茅新進可比，乃亦務為粉飾，於治道人心關係尤鉅。

translations.literal: Now Hongzhang is a governor-general, not comparable to a new scholar; yet he also strives to ornament—this bears especially on governance and popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Li is a governor-general, not a novice scholar, yet he too ornaments reports—a matter that touches governance and public trust.

sentences.zh: 應請降旨訓飭。」

translations.literal: A decree of admonition should be issued."
translations.idiomatic: The throne should issue a reprimand."

sentences.zh: 是時鴻章又以永定河合龍，奏獎工員勞勚，奏上而河復決，寶泉又疏請撤銷保案。

translations.literal: At that time Hongzhang also reported the Yongding River's completion and rewarded the engineers; the memorial went up and the river broke again, and Baoquan again memorialized to revoke the commendation.
translations.idiomatic: About then Li also reported the Yongding River joined and rewarded engineers; the memorial arrived and the river broke again, and Bian asked to revoke the commendations.

sentences.zh: 鴻章新建大功，寶泉再疏彈之，鴻章亦不以為忤，天下兩賢之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang had newly built great merit; Baoquan again memorialized against him, yet Hongzhang did not take offense, and the world praised both as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Li had just won great credit; Bian impeached him again, yet Li took no offense, and the world praised both men.

sentences.zh: 遷戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He became supervising secretary of the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 先是都御史胡家玉疏陳丁漕積弊，語侵巡撫劉坤一，坤一覆奏家玉逋賦未完，且私書囑託公事。

translations.literal: Earlier Censor-in-Chief Hu Jiayu memorialized on accumulated abuses of land tax and tribute grain, his words touching Governor Liu Kunyi; Kunyi replied that Jiayu had not finished paying tax arrears and had privately written recommending official business.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censor-in-Chief Hu Jiayu had exposed grain-tax abuses, implicating Governor Liu Kunyi; Liu replied that Hu still owed taxes and had privately lobbied on official business.

sentences.zh: 寶泉复劾：「坤一藉詞箝制地方長吏，此端一開，啟天下輕視朝廷之漸。」

translations.literal: Baoquan again impeached: "Kunyi uses words to restrain local chief officials; once this begins, it opens the gradual tendency for the empire to slight the court."
translations.idiomatic: Bian impeached again: "Liu Kunyi uses rhetoric to intimidate local magistrates; that opens the way for governors to slight the throne."

sentences.zh: 疏入，坤一下部議處。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Kunyi was sent to the ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached Beijing and Liu was referred to the ministries for discipline.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，出為陝西督糧道，再遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he went out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi, then was promoted to treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu year three sent him as Shaanxi grain commissioner, then treasurer.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine made him Shaanxi governor.

sentences.zh: 尚書閻敬銘議陝西收放糧米改徵折色，寶泉持不可，以謂：「穀數有定，今改折色，所收必有減於昔而民始樂從，所放必加多於前而兵乃足用。

translations.literal: Minister Yan Jingming proposed that Shaanxi's grain collection and disbursement be changed to cash payment; Baoquan held it impossible, saying: "Grain has a fixed amount; if changed to cash, what is collected must be less than before before the people will comply, and what is disbursed must be more than before before troops are supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yan Jingming wanted Shaanxi grain receipts paid in cash; Bian objected: "Grain quotas are fixed; cash collection will yield less than grain while troops need more—

sentences.zh: 入不敷出，一時強為彌補，後將何所取償？

translations.literal: Income will not cover expenditure; forced to patch for a time, how will it be repaid later?
translations.idiomatic: income will not cover outlay; temporary fixes will leave nothing for the next crisis.

sentences.zh: 昔歲大饑，終賴道倉儲粟，多所全活。

translations.literal: In past years of great famine, it was finally the transit granaries' stored grain that saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Past famines were survived only because transit granaries still held grain.

sentences.zh: 今並此而去之，恐饑饉洊臻，益無可恃。」

translations.literal: Now if this too is removed, I fear when famine comes again there will be nothing to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: Remove that reserve and the next famine will find nothing to rely on."

sentences.zh: 上韙其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調河南巡撫，移疾歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to governor of Henan and resigned on illness.
translations.idiomatic: Year twelve transferred him to Henan governor; he soon resigned for illness.

sentences.zh: 二十年，即家起閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was recalled from home as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty recalled him from retirement as Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 閩鹽逋課積八十餘萬，前任奏報，率皆飛灑他項為挹注。

translations.literal: Fujian salt owed more than eight hundred thousand in taxes; former governors' reports always shifted the burden to other items as stopgap.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian salt owed more than eight hundred thousand taels; predecessors had papered over arrears by shifting charges elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 寶泉至，盡發其覆，乃有停釐補課之奏。

translations.literal: When Baoquan arrived he fully exposed the cover-up and then memorialized to suspend likin and make up the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Bian exposed every cover-up and memorialized to suspend likin surcharges until arrears were paid.

sentences.zh: 船政舊設大臣，後以總督兼之。

translations.literal: The naval dockyard had formerly had a dedicated minister, later the governor-general held it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The Foochow Navy Yard once had its own minister; later the governor-general held it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 寶泉特疏請復故制，且條上造船、購料、延教師、籌經費四事，而不私其權，人嘉其廉讓。

translations.literal: Baoquan specially memorialized to restore the old system and listed four items—shipbuilding, purchasing materials, hiring instructors, and raising funds—without keeping power for himself; people praised his integrity and modesty.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to restore the separate minister and listed shipbuilding, supplies, instructors, and funding without hoarding authority; contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒於官，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died in office and was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in year twenty-four and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 於廕霖，字次棠，吉林伯都訥廳人。

translations.literal: Yu Yinlin, style name Citang, was a native of Boduna Subprefecture, Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yinlin, courtesy name Citang, came from Boduna in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng, he became a metropolitan graduate, was changed to Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianfeng, he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 從大學士倭仁問學。

translations.literal: He studied with Grand Secretary Woren.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Grand Secretary Woren.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，俄羅斯議還伊犁，廕霖疏劾崇厚擅許天山界地數百里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, when Russia discussed returning Yili, Yinlin memorialized impeaching Chonghou for unauthorized cession of several hundred li of Tianshan territory.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangxu, when Russia negotiated the return of Yili, Yu impeached Chonghou for ceding hundreds of li of Tianshan territory without authority.

sentences.zh: 及崇厚被逮，有為之遊說者，复嚴疏劾之，且劾樞臣畏葸欺罔。

translations.literal: When Chonghou was arrested, some lobbied for him; he again memorialized sternly against him and also impeached the Grand Council for cowardice and deception.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghou was arrested, lobbyists intervened; Yu memorialized again and also accused the Grand Council of cowardice and deceit.

sentences.zh: 六年，授贊善，累遷中允。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed tutor, and was promoted through junior mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Year six made him a tutor in the heir apparent's establishment; he rose to junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為湖北荊宜施道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as circuit intendant of Jing-Yi-Shi in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight sent him as intendant of the Jing-Yi-Shi circuit in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 是秋淫雨，漢水溢，檄所屬開倉賑濟。

translations.literal: That autumn heavy rain overflowed the Han River; he ordered subordinates to open granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Han River flooded; he ordered granaries opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 又濬紫貝淵上游，改閘為壩，疏支流，洩積潦，水患始息。

translations.literal: He also dredged the upper reaches of Zibei Bay, changed the sluice to a dam, cleared branch channels, and drained accumulated water, and the flood trouble ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Zibei Bay upstream, converted the sluice to a dam, cleared branch channels, drained the backlog, and the floods eased.

sentences.zh: 新荊州書院，設經義、治事兩齋，生徒雲集，講舍至不能容。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the Jingzhou Academy, established two halls for classical learning and practical administration; students gathered until the dormitories could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt Jingzhou Academy with halls for classics and practical administration; students overflowed the dormitories.

sentences.zh: 擒斬盜魁李人奴等，餘黨屏息。

translations.literal: He captured and executed the bandit chief Li Rennu and others; the rest of the gang fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed bandit chief Li Rennu; the gang fell silent.

sentences.zh: 宜昌民教構訟，法領事袒教民，挾兵艦至，廕霖不為動，後卒無事。

translations.literal: At Yichang a civil case between Chinese and Christians went to court; the French consul favored the Christians and brought warships; Yinlin was unmoved and in the end nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: At Yichang a Chinese-Christian lawsuit drew the French consul and gunboats; Yu stood firm and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 英商漏宜昌關稅，既覺，乃納賕請免，不許；

translations.literal: An English merchant evaded Yichang customs duties; when discovered he offered a bribe to be excused, which was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: An English merchant evaded Yichang customs; caught, he offered a bribe and was refused.

sentences.zh: 請補稅，許之。

translations.literal: He asked to pay the tax; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to pay the back taxes.

sentences.zh: 英商歎其廉。

translations.literal: The English merchant praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢廣東按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Year eleven made him Guangdong judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廣東素多盜，至白晝劫掠衢市。

translations.literal: Guangdong had always many bandits; even in daylight they robbed the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong had always been bandit-ridden; robbers struck market streets in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 廕霖言於總督張之洞，奏請就地正法，報可。

translations.literal: Yinlin spoke to Governor-General Zhang Zhidong and memorialized for summary execution on the spot, which was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told Governor-General Zhang Zhidong and won approval for summary execution on the spot.

sentences.zh: 順德廩生簡明亮有學行，緣事繫獄，察其枉，立出之。

translations.literal: Shunde stipend student Jian Mingliang had learning and conduct but was imprisoned on a charge; Yinlin saw he was wronged and released him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde scholar Jian Mingliang, a man of learning, was jailed on false charges; Yu saw the injustice and freed him immediately.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷雲南布政使，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to treasurer of Yunnan and entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Year twelve transferred him to Yunnan treasurer; he left on mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，改授台灣布政使，未行，會弟編修鍾霖以前在籍與廕霖同辦賑務，為奸商湯連魁誣控獲譴，廕霖具疏辨。

translations.literal: After mourning he was reassigned Taiwan treasurer; before departing, his younger brother Compiler Zhonglin had earlier handled relief at home with Yinlin and was falsely accused by merchant Tang Liankui; Yinlin memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was named Taiwan treasurer; before leaving, his brother Zhonglin, who had helped with relief at home, was framed by merchant Tang Liankui; Yu memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 詔遣大臣即訊，頗得連魁行賄狀，然廕霖猶坐是落職，廢居京師。

translations.literal: An edict sent a grand minister to investigate on the spot and obtained proof of Liankui's bribery, yet Yinlin still lost his post for this and lived in retirement in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a grand minister to investigate, proved Tang's bribery, yet Yu still lost his post and lived in retirement in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 二十年，日本戰事起，命往奉天襄依克唐阿軍。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when war with Japan arose, he was ordered to go to Fengtian to assist Yi Ketang'a's army.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty, when war with Japan broke out, he was ordered to Fengtian to assist General Yi Ketang'a.

sentences.zh: 請募兵二萬自效，詔許募萬人，分四軍，與民團相應援。

translations.literal: He asked to raise twenty thousand troops at his own expense; an edict permitted ten thousand in four armies to cooperate with militia.
translations.idiomatic: He offered to raise twenty thousand troops at his own expense; the court allowed ten thousand in four corps cooperating with militia.

sentences.zh: 明年，和議成，總督張之洞、山東巡撫李秉衡交章論薦，詔賞三品頂戴。

translations.literal: The next year when peace was made, Governors-General Zhang Zhidong and Shandong Governor Li Bingheng jointly recommended him; an edict granted third-rank rank.
translations.idiomatic: After peace the next year, Zhang Zhidong and Shandong governor Li Bingheng recommended him; the court granted third rank.
